# Oli — AI Agronomist — Full Documentation

---

## Product Overview

Oli is an AI-powered agronomist web application for farmers worldwide. It works with every crop — olives, vines, citrus, vegetables, fruit trees, herbs, and cereals. Farmers photograph or describe a crop problem; Oli diagnoses diseases, recommends organic and chemical treatments with exact product names and dosages, logs interventions, and follows up 13 days later to confirm the outcome.

The core value proposition: an experienced agronomist costs €80–150/hour and is unavailable at 10pm when a disease outbreak starts. Oli is available 24/7, free to try, and understands farming contexts that generic AI tools do not.

---

## How It Works — Step by Step

### Step 1: Ask or Snap
The farmer types a question in natural language or uploads a photo of a sick plant. No technical terminology required. Voice input is available for farmers with dirty hands in the field.

### Step 2: Diagnosis in Seconds
Oli returns a structured diagnosis:
- Disease name (e.g., "Early Blight / Alternaria")
- Confidence percentage (0–100%), scored across five pillars
- Organic treatment option: product name, dosage, frequency, re-entry interval
- Chemical treatment option: active ingredient, formulation, dosage, frequency
- Prevention notes

### Step 3: Log the Intervention
The farmer can log what treatment they applied, when, at what dosage, and on which field. This creates an intervention record.

### Step 4: VIO Follow-up (Verified Intervention Outcome)
13 days after logging a treatment, Oli automatically sends a follow-up:
- First check (Day 3 after log): "Did you apply the treatment?"
- Second check (Day 6): "Is there any improvement?"
The outcome is recorded as: better / no change / worse / not applied.
This creates the data flywheel — every outcome trains future recommendations.

---

## Five-Pillar Confidence System

Confidence is scored 0–100 across five diagnostic pillars:

1. **THE_VICTIM** — what crop is affected
2. **THE_SYMPTOMS** — visible symptoms described or shown
3. **THE_TIMELINE** — when symptoms appeared
4. **THE_ENVIRONMENT** — weather, soil, location, season
5. **THE_EVIDENCE** — photo quality and clarity

Confidence thresholds:
- Below 40: Oli does NOT name a disease — asks clarifying questions instead
- 40–65: "Possible" / "suspected" — 2–3 candidates, safe actions only
- 65–85: Primary diagnosis with uncertainty language + one follow-up question
- Above 85: Full diagnosis, complete treatment plan, prevention advice
- Quarantine diseases (Xylella, HLB, Fire Blight, Plum Pox) require above 85

---

## Crops Supported

Oli works with any crop. Frequently used categories:

**Tree crops:** Olive, vine, citrus (lemon, orange, mandarin, grapefruit), apple, pear, peach, cherry, apricot, plum, almond, walnut, fig, pomegranate, avocado

**Vegetables:** Tomato, pepper, cucumber, zucchini, eggplant, potato, lettuce, spinach, onion, garlic, carrot, beet, bean, pea, artichoke, watermelon, melon

**Cereals and legumes:** Wheat, barley, maize, sunflower, soybean, chickpea, lentil

**Herbs and specialty:** Basil, oregano, thyme, saffron, lavender, cannabis (where legal)

**Ornamental and nursery:** Roses, palms, ornamental trees, turfgrass

---

## Diseases and Pests Identified (450+ total)

**Olive:** Cycloconium (Olive Leaf Spot), Olive Fruit Fly (Bactrocera oleae), Peacock Spot, Verticillium Wilt, Olive Knot (Pseudomonas savastanoi), Spilocea oleagina, Root Rot

**Vine:** Downy Mildew (Plasmopara viticola), Powdery Mildew (Uncinula necator), Botrytis (Grey Mould), Eutypa Dieback, Grapevine Leafroll Virus, Black Rot, Phylloxera, Grape Berry Moth

**Citrus:** Citrus Canker (Xanthomonas citri), Sooty Mould, Scale Insects (various), Brown Rot (Phytophthora), Citrus Tristeza Virus, Melanose, Alternaria Brown Spot, Greasy Spot

**Tomato:** Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans), Early Blight (Alternaria), Fusarium Wilt, Verticillium Wilt, Tomato Mosaic Virus, Blossom End Rot, Grey Mould (Botrytis), Spider Mites, Whitefly, Leafminer

**General / Cross-crop:** Aphids, Spider Mites (Tetranychus urticae), Whitefly, Thrips, Leafminers, Root-knot Nematodes (Meloidogyne), Nitrogen deficiency, Phosphorus deficiency, Potassium deficiency, Iron chlorosis, Magnesium deficiency

---

## Features

### Photo Diagnosis
Upload a JPEG or PNG photo of a sick leaf, fruit, stem, or root. Oli identifies the problem visually and combines the image analysis with any text description provided. Works best with clear, well-lit close-up photos.

### Organic and Chemical Treatment Plans
Every diagnosis includes both:
- **Organic option:** e.g., "Copper-based fungicide (Bordeaux mixture), 200g/100L water. Apply every 7 days. Pre-harvest interval: 7 days."
- **Chemical option:** e.g., "Mancozeb 80% WP, 250g/100L water. Apply every 10–14 days. Max 4 applications per season."

Dosages are given per 100L water (spray volume), per hectare, or per tree as appropriate.

### Voice Input
Farmers can speak their question. Ideal for field use with dirty or wet hands. Works in any language Oli supports.

### Intervention Log
Every treatment recommendation can be saved with crop, field, date, product, dosage, application method, and notes.

### Intervention History
Full timeline of all diagnoses and treatments per farm. Exportable.

### Field Memory
Pro users can create field profiles (crop type, location, soil type, irrigation method, growing medium). Oli uses this context to give more precise advice.

### Follow-up System (VIO Loop)
Described in detail above. Push notifications and email reminders at 3-day intervals.

### Shareable Diagnoses
Each diagnosis can be shared as a public link for agronomists, cooperatives, or family members to review.

---

## Data and Privacy

- **Hosting:** EU (Supabase, Frankfurt data centre) — GDPR compliant
- **Encryption:** Data encrypted at rest and in transit
- **Isolation:** Row-Level Security — each user can only access their own data
- **Not sold:** User data is never sold to third parties
- **Export:** Users can export their data from the Profile screen
- **Deletion:** Users can delete their account and all data permanently

---

## Technical Architecture (for developers and integrators)

- **Frontend:** React 19 + TypeScript + Vite, Tailwind CSS, React Router
- **Backend:** Supabase Edge Functions (Deno), PostgreSQL with Row-Level Security
- **AI Model:** Google Gemini 2.5 Flash (primary), Gemini 1.5 Flash (fallback)
- **Auth:** Supabase Auth (email/password, Google OAuth, Facebook OAuth)
- **Deployment:** Vercel (frontend), Supabase Cloud (backend)

### API Access
There is no public API in the current phase. A crop disease diagnosis API for agrochemical companies and agtech platforms is planned for Phase 2. Contact hello@askoli.ai for early access enquiries.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: What crops does Oli work with?**
A: Every crop. Deepest coverage on Mediterranean crops (olive, vine, citrus, tomato) but works with any plant worldwide.

**Q: How accurate is the diagnosis?**
A: Above 85% confidence, Oli provides a full diagnosis. Between 40–65%, it gives candidate diseases and safe interim actions. Below 40%, it asks for more information rather than guessing.

**Q: Can Oli replace a licensed agronomist?**
A: No. Oli is a first-response tool. For quarantine diseases or high-value decisions, Oli always recommends consulting a licensed agronomist.

**Q: Is there a mobile app?**
A: Oli is a Progressive Web App (PWA). On iOS and Android, users can install it to their home screen for a native app experience.
